event_requirements.details: Medhas distinguishes eternal Devī from births described when she appears for divine purposes. At cosmic dissolution Viṣṇu sleeps on Śeṣa; Madhu and Kaiṭabha arise from his ear-region and threaten lotus-seated Brahmā.

Brahmā praises the goddess as sacrificial utterance, cosmic creation, preservation and dissolution, knowledge, illusion, nature and armed power. He asks her to delude the demons and awaken Viṣṇu to kill them.

Yoganidrā leaves Viṣṇu’s eyes, mouth, nose, arms, heart and breast and appears before Brahmā. Viṣṇu awakens and fights the demons with his arms for five thousand years; deluded and intoxicated with strength, they offer him a boon.

Viṣṇu chooses their death at his hands. They stipulate a place where earth is not flooded; he accepts and kills them with his discus. The Sanskrit says jaghane, while Pargiter renders the bodily locus ambiguously; a precise thigh-position is reserved for review.
event_requirements.outcome: Madhu and Kaiṭabha are slain under their stated condition.

bounded_excerpts: The exact bodily place associated with the final act is uncertain across the bounded witnesses used for this book. The story therefore keeps only what the cleared evidence establishes
The account gives no childhood for them, no family history and no earlier boon.
they were not a list invented by the storyteller, nor a declaration added by this book.
The source tells of a combat fought with his arms, close and unrelenting.
The account does not bring in another deity to grant it, nor does it tell of an older ascetic bargain that made the demons invulnerable.
The telling does not linger over the violence. It is enough to know
After five thousand years of struggle, there was no third attacker and no further condition. The unusual boon had been offered, chosen, limited and fulfilled.

Yoganidra’s part in the episode was complete: she had held the cosmic sleep, withdrawn when Brahma invoked her, appeared before him, and deluded the two Asuras until their confidence turned the battle.
This bounded tale does not claim when they receded or what came next.

Sage Medhas brought the episode to its close where the source-bounded action closes: the threat to Brahma ended, Madhu and Kaitabha defeated under their own condition, and the power behind sleep revealed through what she had done.
The episode asks readers to notice how its turning points differ from one another.
The story does not treat sleep, strength and wisdom as if they were the same thing. Each has a different place in the sequence.
This is a modern editorial reflection, not a quotation from the Devi Mahatmya and not an additional event in the sacred story.
